inconsistencies.reason: Requirement 38 states that the CEP card must generate a signature during a purchase transaction, whereas 39 states the merchant generates the primary signature and the card plays only a passive validation role.
Requirement 11 states that the POS device initiates the cancel last purchase transaction, while 119 states it can only be initiated by the cardholder without any involvement from the POS device.

Requirement 59 states that the Cancel Last Purchase transaction is performed off-line without card issuer authentication, whereas 121 mandates that it must always be performed online with direct card issuer approval.
Requirement 103 dictates that S1 must be generated entirely by the load device with no card participation, but 123 requires the card to generate S1 using both card and load device data.

Requirement 139 requires the card to maintain a global total balance with a mandatory absolute maximum limit, while 148 explicitly states there is no requirement for the card to maintain a maximum total value.
Requirement 141 mandates a globally shared signature key identical across all cards, whereas 142 requires a unique diversified secret key personalized into each card.

Requirement 113 states the aggregate funds pool must be managed without centralized tracking by the card issuer, but 154 requires the card issuer to reflect all changes in the aggregate funds pool on their own systems.
Requirement 13 restricts the storage of aggregation records exclusively to the card itself, while 181 requires them to be stored in the PSAM and allows storage in the POS device.
Requirement 97 makes the cancel last purchase command optional for POS devices, whereas 174 mandates its support for all transactions with no option to opt out.
Requirement 134 states that the card issuer validates S1, but 184 explicitly forbids the card issuer from doing so, requiring an independent third-party authentication service instead.

Requirement 102 states that S1 generation and transmission must occur after the transaction is completed, while 166 states S1 is sent in an authorization request, which must happen before the transaction completes.

Requirement 156 forbids automated aggregation processes in any POS device or system, whereas 182 requires the PSAM (part of the POS system) to automatically increase the total count and amount for aggregated transactions.
